final_message:
I've rewritten the skill's description. I haven't tested whether agents now load it: I couldn't run sessions in this turn, so it's untested.

**Why it never loaded:** agents decide whether to load a skill from its description alone. The old one was just `Helps with parquet files.` It doesn't say when to use the skill, and it has none of the words an agent would see while writing parquet. Nothing in the skill body tells agents when to load it, so the description is the only thing to fix.

**New description** (`skills/parquet-schema-check/SKILL.md:3`):

> Use when about to write or save a DataFrame to a parquet file (to_parquet, write_parquet, pyarrow write_table), or when a job reading parquet fails on a missing column, wrong dtype, column order or schema mismatch

- It names the moment to load the skill (just before the write) and the function names agents actually call. The second clause catches the later symptom: a reader job failing on a schema error.
- It doesn't describe the steps (compare, stop, don't cast). If it did, agents could follow the description and skip the skill body.
- It's about writing and schema errors, while `polars-lazy-tuning` covers slow or memory-heavy reads. The two shouldn't compete for the same prompts.

**Testing needed before you rely on it:**
1. Write 3 or more prompts that should load the skill, worded the way users write them (e.g. "save this frame to `data/orders.parquet`").
2. Write 3 or more near misses: "speed up this `scan_parquet` query", "read this parquet into pandas".
3. Run each prompt in a fresh session with the old description and again with the new one, and count how often the skill loads. The fix works if loads go up on the first set and don't go up on the near misses.

I can write those prompts if you want, but someone needs to run the sessions.

**Also:**
- Neither skill has a `license` field. The writing-skills guide requires one, but I didn't add it because I don't know your project's license.
- I haven't committed the change.
